criteria.quote: Nidoran♂ Has Ears That Point Anywhere
criteria.revision: Replace the title or first line with: "Nidoran♂'s ears are always upright—but developed muscles let them move freely in any direction."

criteria.quote: Nidoran♂'s ear muscles let it aim both ears in any direction, making even tiny sounds hard to miss.
If its ears catch everything, can anything still surprise Nidoran♂?
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported absolute with: "If Nidoran♂ detects danger with those ears, what does it do next?" Then answer it with the documented fact that it strikes first when it senses danger.

criteria.quote: It keeps scanning, raising those ears above the grass for danger.
criteria.revision: After establishing the ear movement and sound detection, pivot immediately to the documented response: "When Nidoran♂ senses danger, it strikes first—charging and stabbing with its poisonous horn."

criteria.quote: But sensing danger is not safety. It strikes with poison.
criteria.revision: Make the reveal more concrete: "The listening ends in an attack: when Nidoran♂ senses danger, it strikes first, using its horn to inject poison."

criteria.quote: EARS THAT POINT ANYWHERE / MUSCLES CONTROL EACH EAR / THE EARS KEEP SCANNING
criteria.revision: Combine the first two ear-mechanics beats into one reveal, then use the freed beat for a new fact: Nidoran♂ raises its ears out of the grass to scan its surroundings, before pivoting to its poisonous horn.

criteria.quote: Its ears can scan every direction, but the real defense is choosing how to answer danger.
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported idea of "choosing" with a factual resolution: "The ears detect danger right away. The answer is immediate: Nidoran♂ strikes first with a horn that injects poison."

criteria.quote: Better defense: movable ears or a poisonous horn?
criteria.revision: Sharpen the comparison while keeping both sides evidence-safe: "Which matters more for protection: ears that detect danger right away, or a horn that injects poison?"
